rows.reason: Near-identical; 'AWS Bedrock' and 'cron triggers' are slightly clearer, and the semicolon separates the observability additions cleanly.
Leads with a defined metric (end-to-end latency) and a causal 'by moving it onto'; B's 'sped up...by 34%' is vague and awkward.
Reads more smoothly, and 'so new engineers can contribute' is a concrete why compared with the vaguer 'easy onboarding'.
'Researching and implementing' already says it is ongoing, so '(in progress)' is redundant.
'LLM workflow generation' gives context, and 'decomposing a skill into sub-skills' is a clear action-driven decision.
Linear structure (what, data source, stack, why) is easier to skim; B's 'distilling' clause is convoluted.
Metric clearly defined (90% of surveyed users preferred it); A's 'rated 90% satisfaction' is vague and has a stray LaTeX escape.
B's 'live' order-book data conflicts with checking against historical IEX data; A's simulation framing is consistent and credible.
Nearly identical; 'perf counters' is slightly more precise about what was measured.
'Replaying historical IEX data' is more precise about what the simulator does; the plug-in clause is equally clear.
Metric is clearly defined (generated meals rated satisfactory by internal testers); B's '(in progress)' repeats what 'Building' already says.
Concrete tooling beats the buzzwords 'scaled' and 'agile teams'; 'has shipped' reads as more honest.
Cleanly separates the work and its purpose from the product's traction; A misplaces the 'to reduce DB load' clause after the visit count.
Semicolon plus 'added' keeps the profiling and tests from being credited with the 30% setup gain; more honest attribution.
'On a PhD-led team' states the candidate's role more accurately than the ambiguous 'with a PhD team'.
